newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commission buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commission buying.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended higher on commission buying and active spreading, traders said.

"RBC-DS bought May and July, 500 May-July spread, locals took profits in the July and there were commission buy stops at $380 in the November," a trader said. July WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -9.22 Wednesday from -10.67 Tuesday. About 500 May-July spread from $6 to $6.30, May-Nov $35.10, May-Aug $2.50. Volume was 4,525 lots with 207 hedges.

Japan bought 4,000-5,000 tonnes canola overnight, sources said. July canola closed up $0.60 at $422.50 and November settled $1.10 higher at $380.30. May flax fell $1.40 to $342.60 and July closed $0.60 lower at $342.20.
Growing concern about flooding in southern Manitoba and the possible effects on the area's crops, limited losses on the WCE. Wheat, barley, canola and flaxseed are grown there.

July feed wheat settled $0.10 higher at $171.50 and October up $0.60 to $170.90 on local and commercial selling while commission houses bought across the board. Alberta Wheat Pool bought December up $1.20 at $169.70 from locals, traders said. Volume was 401 lots.

May western barley fell $0.50 to $140.70. July closed $0.30 lower at $140.50 as hedge selling met with commission buying. About 370 May-July spread from even money to $0.40, 40 Oct-Dec at even money, 150 July-Dec at $0.80. Volume was 1,600 lots.
May feed peas traded unchanged at US$217 on commission demand and October rose US$0.50 to US$198.40 on commercial buying. Volume was 90 lots. Oats did not trade.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
